result.rationale: The diff's parseRefreshTokenResponse explicitly sets `refreshTokenResponse.data.refresh_token = "refresh_token"` when sync mode is on, and callers (e.g. googlecalendar CalendarService `key = parseRefreshTokenResponse(googleCredentials, ...)` followed by `prisma.credential.update({ data: { key } })`) persist that value into credential.key. If APP_CREDENTIAL_SHARING_ENABLED/CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT is later removed, refresh flows will POST the literal placeholder as the refresh token, breaking token refresh until re-authorization. The mechanism is fully visible in the diff.

judged_text: The function overwrites a missing refresh_token with the literal placeholder string 'refresh_token', and callers persist this placeholder into credential.key in place of the real refresh token. A self-hoster who enables credential sharing (sync mode supplies only access tokens) and later disables it is left with credentials whose refresh_token is the literal string 'refresh_token', so reverting to normal OAuth refresh fails for every affected user until they manually re-authorize each app.
